evidence: A personal trip-report blog places Ellen Pea on the south-facing Supercave granite wall above Highway 20 near Washington Pass, so no glacier is anywhere near the line; no snow is described on a June-September ascent.
Searches found only general Emerald Peak pages (Entiat/Chelan area) and a May snow-slope report on a neighbouring peak; nothing describing this line, so the proposal stands unconfirmed.

The AAC route note puts it on Prusik Peak's south face, and trip reports for Prusik show a snow-free, dry peak by September with snow only on the long approach early in the year; no glacier is involved.
Mountaineers trip reports for the Teanaway Esmeralda Peaks describe June snow filling the upper basin up to the col and gullies; they mention no glacier. Season is June only so snow stays in season.

A Wenatchee outdoors write-up and SummitPost log call the standard line a class 2 scramble with no glacier; snow in the gullies helps in June, best window mid-June to mid-July, after which it is loose scree.

Mountain Project and a Cascade Climbers report describe an approach over snow and talus to the base of Stuart's west wall, with no glacier named, but nothing states the full line or when the base is dry, so it stays unsure.
Mountain Project places the route on Guye's west face above a talus cone near Snoqualmie Pass, so no glacier; the sources found were winter reports and none gave a melt-out date for the cone.

A Cascade Climbers June report on Half Moon's north ridge says the notch slope is easy on snow and turns to loose scree as it melts, no glacier; it gives no date, and the match to this route is not certain.
Mountaineers trip reports from July 15 and August 4 found the approach nearly snow free with avoidable patches between the lake and the notch, ice axes unused; no glacier is on this ridge.

Mountaineers reports show snow on the ridge in late June, a snow-free summit gully on July 12 in one year but snow crossed in July 2010 in a late year, and all snow gone by mid-August; no glacier. Moved the date later.

Mountaineers route page and trip reports describe crampons and axe in the notch gully early, with significant snow on the pass and notch approach reported in July of 2016 and 2020; no glacier. Moved the date later than July 1.

Mountaineers and trail reports show the PCT snow-covered in May and June and still numerous snow fields near the Katwalk in early July 2024; a plain trail scramble with no glacier, so the date goes to August 1.
Only a Mountain Project listing row ties it to Colchuck Balanced Rock in the Enchantments; no description of the approach, descent or snow was found, so glacier and date are unconfirmed.
The Mountaineers route page and SummitPost say the approach gully is usually snow filled and icy until late June; no glacier is on the Liberty Bell southwest face.
It uses the same Beckey approach gully, which the Mountaineers page says is snow filled until late June; no glacier on the southwest face.
The Mountaineers northwest face page exists but its approach snow timing was not read; assumed to match the Beckey gully (snow until late June) and no glacier on Liberty Bell.
Shares the Beckey gully approach, which Mountaineers and SummitPost both say holds snow until late June; no glacier.
Mountaineers pages describe a class 3-4 rock ridge with a Cave Ridge approach and no glacier; spring and May reports met steep snow while a July party never touched snow.
No peak by this name turned up in searches (only Massie Lake in the Glacier Peak area near Suiattle Pass), so there is no basis to clear glacier or give a date; date removed.
Mountaineers, Cascade Climbers and WTA reports on the south gully show variable snow and cornice-like formations, axe sometimes unnecessary; no glacier described, south-facing so early melt.
Mountaineers, WTA and SummitPost pages describe a rough-path scramble from Boulder Lake with no glaciers mentioned; one September report found only scree, but no source gave a melt-out date.
Country High Points and other personal reports describe Ballard snow in October at the col and east ledge; no glacier is mentioned but nothing covers July to September conditions on the south slopes.
A Cascade Climbers report records the first ascent on August 23, 2011 on the east face of Bigelow in the Sawtooth, with no snow or glacier mentioned.
